surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between −NH2 and Si−Cl bonds, followed by the formation of −Si−NH−Si− and −Si−NH2 groups under NH3 plasma exposure.
evidence: Figure 5 represents the proposed reaction pathway of PEALD SiNx using HCDS and 3CDS on the surface terminated with amine groups. In this case, the surface coverage of single −NH−SiCl2−SiH3 can be reduced because of the smaller atomic size of hydrogen. The molecular structure of 3CDS leads to additional adsorption on the adjacent −NHx groups sites because of the low hindrance effect, so that the amount of unreacted hydrogen can be effectively reduced. In addition, stronger physisorption of the 3CDS on the surface can be expected because of its relatively higher dipole moments (Table S1). Eventually, the less steric hindrance and the higher dipole−dipole interaction of the 3CDS can significantly improve the effective surface coverage during precursor exposure.
